1.title: Five civil police officers are killed in an Israeli airstrike in al-Mawasi, Rafah, Gaza Strip. Separately, three more Palestinians, including a four-year-old child, are killed in an airstrike on a building in Gaza City.
Bolivian president Rodrigo Paz declares a national state of emergency to mobilize resources before the super El Niño event peaks in November or December.
Nine people are killed after a Learjet 60 business jet bound for The Bahamas crashes in Greenacres, Florida, United States.
Four workers are killed after entering a food waste tank at a hotel in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, India.

The government of Delhi, India, introduces stricter pollution controls, including double parking fees, remote work arrangements, restrictions on high-emission vehicles, and bans on dust-producing construction, as PM2.5 levels reach 201 mic…

Portuguese riot police dismantle protest camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square and Porto, arresting 13 people for refusing orders to disperse. Thirteen officers are injured, while activists say more than 30 protesters are also injured.

2.title: Israeli forces withdraw from areas around Hebron in the occupied West Bank after a multi-day operation following the killing of two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint.
The United States military carries out airstrikes on Iranian targets across the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian surface-to-air missiles attack American aircraft in the Strait.

Russian forces drop at least nine bombs on a school building serving as a civilian shelter and humanitarian aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine, killing at least 33 people and leaving 50 others missing.
Salvadoran, Haitian, and Gang Suppression Force soldiers launch an offensive in Plain of the Cul-de-Sac which extends from Haiti to the Dominican Republic, killing at least a dozen gang members.
Three people are killed and five more injured in two separated mass shootings at two drug rehabilitation centers in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico.
The Rapid Support Forces launches drone strikes against three distribution stations in Sudan's Kassala and Northern states.

3.title: A commercial vessel is hit by an unidentified object in the waters of Musandam Governorate, Oman, killing an Indian crew member, while 13 others are rescued.
A 21-year-old garment worker dies from injuries sustained the previous day during violent clashes with law enforcement in Gazipur.
Ten police officers are injured in clashes between police and garment workers in Dhaka over low pay and the rising cost of living.

Unidentified attackers ambush a police convoy near Gidan-Giye village in Zamfara State, Nigeria, killing at least five police officers and three members of the Zamfara Community Protection Guard, injuring two officers, and abducting an uns…
Spanish author Cristina Fernández Cubas is awarded the 2026 Cervantes Prize to honor her writing in the Spanish language.

The Reserve Bank of Australia raises its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85%, its highest level since 2008, citing persistent inflation and rising energy costs associated with the Iran war.

4.title: Over 50 people are injured and police vehicles are torched as garment workers clash with police in Savar.
Two women are killed in a airstrike by Sudan's army on a water source in Umm Badr, North Kordofan.

The Bangladeshi garment industry wage board agrees to increase minimum wages following five days of worker protests and clashes with police. Workers demand ৳30,000 (US$240) monthly, up from ৳12,500 (US$100), while the board has not specifi…
Five people are killed while two others are injured in an explosion at a suspected illegal fireworks factory in Malasiqui, Pangasinan, Philippines.
A fire and explosion at a Panasonic subsidiary's factory in Hsinchu County, Taiwan, kills two employees and injures five others.

The Singaporean parliament amends the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act of 2014, introducing arrest powers, permitting trials in absentia, and increasing maximum fines tenfold to S$20 million (US$15 million) following widespread air polluti…

5.title: A police officer is killed and another injured in a stabbing attack outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Amman, Jordan. The suspect is arrested. The event is described as a terrorist attack.
Mexico approves the Digital Economy Act for Digital and Electronic Payments, which allows it to designate sectors in which digital payments are the only accepted means of payment.
Eleven people are killed and 33 more injured after the collision of a passenger bus with a truck in Pakpattan District, Punjab, Pakistan.
Six people are killed and nine more injured after a fire at a two-story home in Brooklyn, New York City, United States.
Six more people are found dead under the debris of a building that collapsed two weeks ago in Nairobi, Kenya, bringing the death toll to eight. Sixteen others are still missing.
Eight people are killed and another is injured in a shooting spree at three separated locations in Afyonkarahisar Province, Turkey. The perpetrator is arrested.

6.title: The death toll from an armed attack yesterday by suspected Allied Democratic Forces militants on several villages in North Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, rises to 33.
Saudi Arabia launches an airstrike against a market in Taiz Governorate, Yemen, killing 30 people and wounding eight more.
Politician Julio Portillo and three police officers are killed in an assassination shooting in Río Hondo, Zacapa Department, Guatemala, by unknown gunmen.
Three gunmen were killed after an encounter against authorities in the ejido Las Trancas, Navolato, Sinaloa, México.

Edgar Aarón Vázquez, founder and leader of the Nuevo Imperio cartel, is killed in an operation in Naucalpan, State of Mexico. He was implicated in the murder of a federal agent, as well as kidnapping, extortion, homicide, dispossession of …
Australia deploys a C-130 Hercules aircraft, a Cessna Citation aircraft, and 20 personnel to help extinguish wildfires in East Kalimantan, Indonesia.

7.title: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) says that they have recaptured the town of Iyal Bakhit in West Kordofan, Sudan. The SAF also reportedly downs a Rapid Support Forces drone.

Six people are killed and 15 more injured in a drive-by mass shooting in the center of Kraków, Poland. The perpetrator, who also killed his parents and his sister at their home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, is wounded by police and arrested.
Saudi airstrikes hit homes near Sanaa, Yemen, killing at least 27 people and wounding 36 others.
A drone strike of unknown origin is launched against a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolívar Department, Colombia, killing three soldiers and wounding 16 more.
A family of twelve are killed in an arson attack during a bandit raid in Maradun, Zamfara State, Nigeria. Seven others are kidnapped.
At least 12 people are injured in Jamalganj, Sunamganj, Bangladesh, during a clash between two factions of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party at a National Revolution and Solidarity Day program.

8.title: At least five people are killed, including four children, and several injured people are rescued after heavy rain and flooding caused a sandbank to collapse in Deir el-Balah, Gaza.

Several floors of Aramco Tower, a skyscraper owned by Saudi Aramco located in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, are damaged after a Houthi ballistic missile is intercepted over the city by Saudi air defense systems. No casualties or injuries are repor…
Iranian state media reports that explosions are heard on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz after reporting that the U.S. military fired projectiles.

Production is temporarily suspended at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan after a liquefied petroleum gas storage tank at the site is hit by a drone. No group claims responsibility for the attack.

Mexican Navy personnel, working with intelligence from the National Intelligence Center and the United States Drug Enforcement Administration, arrest Rafael Álvarez Ayala, the alleged leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel cell "Los R…
At least 10 people are injured in Araihazar, Narayanganj, Bangladesh, during a clash between two factions of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party at a National Revolution and Solidarity Day program.

9.title: The Wall Street Journal reports that the United States has evacuated aircraft from the RAF Mildenhall base in the United Kingdom, citing threats from Iran.

The 24-year-old man responsible for the drive-by mass shooting at the Main Square in Kraków, Poland, two days ago, which killed six people and injured 16 others, dies at a hospital after being seriously wounded in a shootout with police.
English author M. John Harrison wins the 2026 Booker Prize for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything.

The Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford, England, United Kingdom, returns the remains of 39 Naga people, collected during the British Raj, to a delegation from Nagaland, India, following six years of discussions over repatriation.
Paraguayan president Pedro Alliana appoints economist Jorge Schreiner to lead the central bank following Ueno Bank's collapse. The Senate approves Schreiner's appointment.

The Chinese commerce ministry extends the suspension of export restrictions on certain rare earths, industrial diamonds, and lithium battery technology to January 10, 2027, amid ongoing trade negotiations with the United States.

10.title: A third round of United States-mediated talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations begins in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, focusing on the humanitarian impact of the war, prisoners of war, and security guarantees. Earlier in the da…
El Salvador announces it has launched a joint military operation with the Haitian police against the 400 Mawozo gang, killing 20 people and destroying a house linked to its leader, Wilson Joseph.

A military court in Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, sentences 66 soldiers to death on charges of cowardice, mutiny, and failure to obey orders, after they were arrested following clashes with Front for the Refoundation …

Eight people, including five workers and two police reservists, are killed by suspected al-Shabaab militants in Mandera County, Kenya, near the border with Somalia, during an ambush against a vehicle.

The Venezuelan National Assembly unanimously approves a reform of the electricity law which allows private companies and joint ventures to invest in the nationalised electricity sector, which the government has controlled since 2007.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore launches a gold reserve service for foreign central banks, international financial institutions, and sovereign entities, and announces expanded tax exemptions for wholesale gold services.

11.title: Iran attacks ship navigation systems on Didamar Island, Oman. Unknown damage is caused.

Israel launches an airstrike against the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, killing six Palestinians, including a surgeon, and wounding over 20 more. Four more people are also killed in other airstrikes in the Gaza Strip.
At least 22 people are killed by Islamic State-affiliated Allied Democratic Forces rebels across eight locations in Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Three Central Reserve Police Force personnel are injured after militants open fire on a checkpoint near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, India. Security forces launch a search operation to locate the attackers.
Pakistani Taliban carries out an ambush against police personnel in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing ten officers. Eighteen gunmen are also killed in the ensuing shootout.
At least 50 garment factories shut down in Savar and Ashulia, as police use tear gas and stun grenades to disperse striking workers blocking roads.

12.title: Haitian and Salvadoran soldiers take control of the Stade Sylvio Cator in Port-au-Prince after two years of gang control.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and United States special envoy Jared Kushner announce that European representatives will join future peace negotiations with Russia, which Russian president Vladimir Putin agrees to while maintainin…

At least ten people are injured, including five with gunshot wounds, during a clash involving gunfire and crude bomb explosions between two factions of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party in Munshiganj Sadar, Dhaka Division, Bangladesh.

Guatemala receives the remains of 1967 Nobel Prize in Literature recipient Miguel Ángel Asturias from France, where he lived, 52 years after his death. President Bernardo Arévalo attends a ceremony ahead of the writer's burial in Guatemala…

Jensen Huang resigns as chief executive officer (CEO) and president of Nvidia and leaves the company's board following reports of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese intelligence agent. Chief financial off…
Over 200 garment factories shut down as workers block the Dhaka–Tangail Highway in Gazipur, leading police to fire stun grenades at the protesting workers.

13.title: Iran says it has destroyed an early-warning radar in Bahrain as a retaliation for a United States strike on telecommunication infrastructure on Bandar Sirik in Hormozgan province.
An encounter between Mexican soldiers and CJNG members leave six gunmen dead in a rural area of Silao, Guanajuato, México.

The United States Federal Aviation Administration issues a nationwide ground stop for all flights due to "extraordinary circumstances involving communications failures". It is lifted four hours later and resulted in the cancellation of app…
A tanker and the cruise ship American Heritage collide in the Mississippi River of the United States. All passengers and crew aboard both ships survive, with 32 people hospitalized for injuries.
Twenty-six people are killed and eleven more are injured in a vehicle collision in Golaghat, Assam, India.
Six people are killed and five more injured after an under-construction building partially collapses in Nairobi, Kenya.

14.title: The Iranian military attacks an American military facility in Bahrain with drones and missiles in one of the largest attacks on the country in months.

Ahmed Abdallah Bishr, the general chief of staff for the Gathering of Sudan Liberation Forces (GSLF), dies from wounds suffered a month ago during an assassination attack by drone strike against his home in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan.
The Philippines wins the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia held in Bangkok, Thailand with the song "Sobra-Sobra" by Carmelle.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association threatens to indefinitely close textile factories without pay under the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006, after ongoing wage protests force the shutdown of 55 units and halt producti…

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney announces that negotiations for a free-trade agreement with the Philippines to eliminate more than 90% of tariff lines have concluded, with signing expected in 2027.
A bus overturns on the Garzón–Neiva highway in Colombia, killing six people and wounding eleven more.

15.title: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that a supertanker carrying two million barrels of oil has sunk in the Strait of Hormuz after striking a naval mine.

Israeli military says that Al-Qassam Brigades commander Samir Abu Younis of the Rafah brigade, who helped plan and oversaw the October 7 attacks on Israel, was killed in a airstrike in the southern area of Gaza Strip, with Hamas confirming…

Three Palestinians are killed and others are injured in shelling and shooting attacks by Israeli troops in various areas of the Gaza Strip, in a continuation of the violation of the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025.
Three people are killed and several others are abducted in a cattle raid in Rabah, Sokoto State, Nigeria.

The Nigerian Defence Headquarters announces that the Nigerian Army killed eight terrorists, arrested 22 additional terrorists, logistical personnel, and their families, and rescued 125 kidnapping victims in various raids in the states of A…

A report released by the Human Rights and Conflict Dynamics Observatory of Indepaz confirms that 45 community leaders and human rights activists, eight former FARC commanders who signed the 2016 peace deal and 87 more people were killed in…

16.title: Saudi Arabia's King Salman appoints Chairman of the General Staff Fayyadh Al Ruwaili as commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, following the retreat of Yemeni government forces from areas near the Bab al-Mandeb to Aden.

Ukraine finishes search and rescue operations at a humanitarian aid distribution center in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, that was destroyed by a Russian airstrike on 2 November. A total of 72 people were killed, and four more people a…

The Crimean Bridge is struck by a Ukrainian kamikaze drone, damaging the structure and prompting Russian authorities to close the bridge to vehicle traffic. The bridge is partially reopened later in the day.
Five gunmen are killed after a shootout between criminal organizations in Chignahuapan, Puebla, Mexico.
Two people are killed and three more injured in a mass shooting at a party in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico.

Around ten people are injured, several requiring hospitalization, in East London, United Kingdom, when banned Awami League activists allegedly attack Bangladeshi expatriates and students with glass bottles and steel rods outside a receptio…

17.title: Five Palestinians are killed, including a child, and others are injured in a series of Israeli airstrikes on various areas of the Gaza Strip, Palestine.

A 72-year-old Palestinian woman is killed and ten others are injured in an attack by Israeli settlers on Palestinian homes in the village of Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank.
Bahrain's military intercepts a number of drones fired by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) at Sheikh Isa Air Base.
The United States Air Force conducts a series of at least six strikes on Qeshm Island. The IRGC says it shot down a General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper drone south of the island.

The Crimean Bridge is struck by Ukrainian drones for the second day in a row, killing two people and prompting Russian authorities to close vehicle traffic again. Open-source intelligence report that a section of the road bridge damaged ye…

Following the arrest of party leaders, banned Awami League and Chhatra League activists mobilize via mosque loudspeakers to storm and burn a police station in Tungipara, Gopalganj District, Bangladesh. Amid police tear gas and rubber bulle…

18.title: The Crimean Bridge connecting Taman, Russia, and Kerch, Russian-occupied Crimea, is struck by Ukrainian forces for the third time in four days, prompting Russian authorities to close the bridge to all traffic.
Salvadoran forces destroy a house belonging to Jeff Larose, the leader of the Taliban gang that operates in Canaan, Haiti. The Gang Suppression Force says it was not involved.
Two Bangladesh Nationalist Party members are killed when suspected members of the banned Awami League attack a motorcycle procession in Narail District, Bangladesh.

A crowd led by Chatra Dal members storms and sets fire to the residence of former Awami League Member of Parliament Shamim Osman in Narayanganj District, while unidentified attackers loot and set fire to two houses belonging to former Mini…

In Gopalganj District, armed members of the banned Awami League, Chhatra League, and Jubo League detonate crude bombs and set fire to a private clinic owned by BNP Member of Parliament K M Babar of Gopalganj-2, forcing patients to evacuate…

The Israeli army launches its first operation in central Gaza Strip amid the displacement of families from the area, for the first time since the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025 came into effect.

19.title: Iran's navy says that an oil tanker caught on fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz.
The Israeli Air Force strikes a Hezbollah underground facility in Lebanon's Bekaa valley.
Two Israeli drones explode in Nabatieh, Lebanon, without causing any injuries.
The Houthis fire missiles at King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which damage the Public Investment Fund Tower and other buildings but cause no injuries.

The Yemeni government's military says it has killed or injured 144 Houthi fighters during recent operations in the Taiz, Marib, and Al-Jawf governorates, and to have repelled an attack in the Tur Al Bahah area.
The Houthis say that Saudi-led coalition airstrikes have killed 10 people in Sanaa, Yemen, over the past two days.

20.title: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations report that an oil tanker has been damaged and caught fire off Khasab, Oman, while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz.
The Saudi-led coalition launches airstrikes on Hodeidah, Yemen, targeting weapons smuggling used by the Houthis, and on targets in the Sanaa, Saada, and Taiz governorates.
Yemeni government forces say they have conducted operations in the Al-Jawf, Marib, and Taiz governorates that have killed or injured 193 Houthi fighters.

A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile strikes a field near the village of Nowy Lipowiec in Lublin Voivodeship, Poland, around 60 miles from a Coalition of the Willing training excercise. Air raid alerts are issued in Lublin and Podkarpackie Voiv…
Three Salvadoran soldiers are killed and another is injured when explosives they are handling detonate.
The governments of Haiti and El Salvador agree to build three new prisons to incarcerate Haitian gang members.

21.title: Three Palestinians are killed by an Israeli drone strike on a food-carrying vehicle in Gaza City, while another is killed by gunfire in Jabalia.
Saudi forces intercept three ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, by the Houthis.
A bombing against a FARC dissidents camp in a rural area of Mapiripán, Meta Department, kills five guerrilla fighters.

Authorities confirm a federal operation in Guasave, Sinaloa, in which Fausto Isidro Meza Flores (a.k.a "El Chapo Isidro") was arrested, that four soldiers were killed and ten wounded as well as sixteen gunmen killed in the operation.
The Finnish defence ministry imposes temporary airspace and maritime restrictions after a drone struck a Russian cargo vessel in international waters of the Gulf of Finland, causing a fire.

Clashes between Bangladesh Nationalist Party supporters and banned Awami League activists in Bera Upazila, Pabna District, injure several people following an arson attack at the abandoned home of former Deputy Speaker Shamsul Hoque Tuku an…

22.title: Bahrain announces that two people were injured by Iranian strikes the previous day.

Several people are killed and at least 10 others are injured after the Russian corvette Merkury is struck by a Ukrainian naval drone attack while docked at the port of Benghazi, Libya. The Merkury later capsizes and sinks.
A Maltese-flagged ship is also struck by naval drones off the coast of Benghazi in the Mediterranean Sea.
The 63rd Golden Horse Awards take place in Taipei, Taiwan, with the Hong Kong film We Are Born Good winning Best Narrative Feature.

Several garment factories in Gazipur, Bangladesh declare holidays amid ongoing minimum wage protests, as clashes erupt between workers and police along the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway, with workers throwing bricks and police firing tear gas a…

Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 95 platoons across seven districts, including two battalions in Gopalganj, stepping up surveillance at key installations and industrial zones using drones and police body cameras.

23.title: The Supreme Court of Spain grant an amnesty to the former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont, who is currently in ‘self-imposed exile’, thereby bringing the legal proceedings against the leaders of the October 2017 declaration of independ…
